sentiment.rationale: The document reports a solid operational quarter with revenue up 18% and improved margins, but forward guidance is not explicitly raised; management reaffirms production rate plans and expresses confidence in the recovery plan while flagging tariff and China delivery risks. The tone is cautiously optimistic but the lack of a clear upward guidance revision keeps the score near neutral, slightly positive due to the strong start and conservative plan that can absorb headwinds.

summary.revenue: $19.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year, primarily reflecting higher commercial delivery volume.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.16) and core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($0.49), improved from ($0.56) and ($1.13) respectively in the prior year.
summary.guidance: Management reaffirms production rate plans: 737 to reach 38 per month this year, 787 to increase to 7 per month, 777X first delivery in 2026. Free cash flow guidance for the year is not adjusted; second half expected to turn positive. China delivery risk is acknowledged but expected to be offset by strong demand elsewhere.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin of 2.4% (up from -0.5% YoY); core operating margin of 1.0% (up from -2.3% YoY). Commercial Airplanes operating margin of -6.6% (improved from -24.6%). Defense, Space & Security operating margin of 2.5% (up from 2.2%). Global Services operating margin of 18.6% (up from 18.2%).
key_risks: Tariffs on imports from Japan and Italy (10% currently) affecting wide-body components; potential for retaliatory tariffs, especially from China, impacting deliveries.
Approximately 50 China deliveries at risk; customers in China have indicated they will not take delivery due to tariffs.
Seat certification issues affecting some 787 deliveries expected to be a challenge for the balance of the year.
Potential for additional countries to impose retaliatory tariffs, expanding beyond China.
Supply chain continuity risk due to tariff disputes; need to manage supplier pricing and avoid disruptions.
Pending acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems and associated risks.
key_opportunities: Strong demand environment: backlog of $545 billion, commercial programs sold out into the next decade.
Production rate increases planned for 737 (to 38/month, then 42, 47, 52) and 787 (to 7/month, then double-digit).
F-47 next-generation fighter contract win secures fighter franchise for decades.
Divestiture of Digital Aviation Solutions for $10.55 billion strengthens balance sheet and focuses on core businesses.
Improved operational performance: 50% reduction in traveled work, 25% reduction in rework hours on 737 line.
Global Services continues strong performance with 18.6% operating margin.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Kelly Ortberg stated 'our recovery plan is in full swing and showing signs that it's being effective' and 'I feel really good about our overall plan for the year,' reflecting confidence despite acknowledged risks.
